record.paper_title: Some open problems in spectral theory
record.original_question: Let A be a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space. For a finite-dimensional subspace L of Dom(A), define the second-order relative spectrum Spec2(A,L) as the set of complex numbers z for which there exists a nonzero u in L such that ((A - zI)u,(A - zI)v)=0 for every v in L. Given a sequence (L_k) of finite-dimensional approximation subspaces, is it true that the limiting second-order relative spectra lim_{k->infinity} Spec2(A,L_k) contain the whole spectrum Spec(A), rather than only the isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity known to be contained in the limit?

evidence.quote: M. Levitin & ES, 2004: Let L be a finite dimensional subspace of Dom(A). Then z ∈ C is said to belong to Spec2(A,L) if there exists u ∈ L \ {0} such that ((A − zI)u,(A − zI)v) = 0, ∀v ∈ L.
L. Boulton, 2006: lim k→∞ Spec2(A,Lk ) ⊇ {isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity}. Question: Is it true that lim k→∞ Spec2(A,Lk ) ⊇ Spec(A)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a self-adjoint (in general unbounded) operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with domain $\mathrm{Dom}(A)$, and let $\mathrm{Spec}(A) \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ denote its spectrum. For any finite-dimensional subspace $L \subseteq \mathrm{Dom}(A)$, define the second-order relative spectrum of $A$ with respect to $L$ by
$$\mathrm{Spec}_2(A,L) := \{ z \in \mathbb{C} : \exists\, u \in L \setminus \{0\} \text{ with } \langle (A-zI)u, (A-zI)v\rangle = 0 \text{ for all } v \in L \}.$$
Equivalently, $z \in \mathrm{Spec}_2(A,L)$ iff the compression of $(A-zI)^2$ to $L$ is singular. Let $(L_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces of $\mathrm{Dom}(A)$ whose union is dense in $H$ (in the graph norm of $A$). Define the limit set
$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathrm{Spec}_2(A,L_k) := \{ z \in \mathbb{C} : \exists\, z_k \in \mathrm{Spec}_2(A,L_k) \text{ with } z_k \to z \}.$$
It is known that this limit set contains every isolated eigenvalue of $A$ of finite multiplicity. Determine whether, for every such sequence $(L_k)$, one has
$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathrm{Spec}_2(A,L_k) \supseteq \mathrm{Spec}(A).$$
artifact.category_tag: Second-order relative spectra of self-adjoint operators
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been resolved in the negative: Shargorodsky (2012/2013) showed that second-order relative spectra do not in general approximate the whole essential spectrum of a bounded self-adjoint operator, so the inclusion of the full spectrum in the limit set fails in general. Earlier work by Boulton established the positive direction only for isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity.

status_evidence.title: On the limit behaviour of second order relative spectra of self-adjoint operators
status_evidence.snippet: Second order relative spectra do not in general approximate the whole of the essential spectrum of a bounded self-adjoint operator.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured inclusion fails: the limit of second-order relative spectra does not in general capture the essential spectrum.

status_evidence.title: J. Spectr. Theory 2 (2012), 293–320
status_evidence.snippet: Limit of second order relative spectra contains isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity but not the essential spectrum in general.
status_evidence.claim: Published resolution showing the inclusion of the full spectrum fails.
